data.name: search_codebook
data.text:
dashboard (pattern · monitor) — Dashboard: Several metrics and states on one view, arranged to be scanned at a glance and drilled into. [aka KPI board, control panel, overview dashboard]
recommendations (pattern · search) — Recommendations: Items proposed by the system from a person’s behaviour, context or the current item, rather than from a query. [aka recommended for you, related items, shelves]
booking-flow (pattern · transact) — Booking flow: Choosing a time, place or seat from what is available, then reserving it. [aka reservation, appointment booking, ticketing]
checkout (pattern · transact) — Checkout: The flow that turns a cart into a paid order: contact, delivery, payment and review. [aka purchase flow, payment flow]

data.name: search_codebook
data.text: data-table (pattern · browse-collections) — Data table: Items as rows against attributes as columns, built for scanning, comparing, sorting, filtering and acting on many items at once. [aka data grid, table view, details view]

data.name: search_codebook
data.text:
version-history (pattern · collaborate) — Version history: A browsable record of past states of an artifact, with authorship, so a person can compare, restore or branch from an earlier version. [aka revision history, timeline of changes, checkpoints]
gantt-timeline (pattern · schedule) — Gantt timeline: Tasks or phases as bars on a horizontal time axis, often with dependencies, progress and a hierarchical work breakdown beside the bars. [aka Gantt chart, project timeline, roadmap timeline, bar schedule]
timeline-editor (pattern · create) — Timeline editor: Composing time-based media by arranging clips on tracks against a time axis. [aka non-linear editor, NLE, sequencer, arrangement view]
activity-log (pattern · monitor) — Activity log: A time-ordered record of what happened to an object or account, and who did it. [aka audit log, history, changelog, event timeline]
undo (component · transact) — Undo: Reversing recent actions. [aka undo and redo, history, revert]
feed (pattern · browse-collections) — Feed: An unbounded, continuously arriving stream of heterogeneous items, ordered by time or by ranking and consumed by scrolling. [aka stream, timeline, activity stream, news feed]
annotation (pattern · collaborate) — Annotation: Attaching discussion or marks to a region of a shared artifact so feedback stays anchored to what it is about. [aka comments, pinned notes, margin notes]
browse-collections (archetype) — Browse collections: Scan many comparable things, narrow to the relevant few, and focus on one — the activity behind shopping, inboxes, file systems and search results alike. [aka collection browsing, information foraging]
overview-detail (pattern · browse-collections) — Overview–detail: An overview of many items, each shown through a few key attributes, paired with a detail view that shows many or all attributes of a selected item. [aka master–detail, director–detail, list–detail, ODI]
view-switcher (component · browse-collections) — View switcher: A control that changes how the same collection is represented. [aka layout toggle, views]
settings (pattern · configure) — Settings: A durable catalog of options that change how an app, account or device behaves, usually revisited rarely and in parts. [aka preferences, options, system settings]
document-editor (pattern · create) — Document editor: Composing a flowing, structured document of text and embedded media. [aka word processor, rich-text editor, block editor]

data.text:
## tabs — Tabs (component, archetype navigate)
A set of peer views sharing one space, one visible at a time, switched by labelled controls.
Aliases: tab bar, segmented control, tab strip
Anatomy: Tab (One label); Panel (The view it shows); Indicator (Which is current)
Related — uses: badge, menu | neighbors: view-switcher, accordion, carousel
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Placement and overflow [layout] — Where are tabs, and what happens when there are too many?
  - placement (single-select: one id) — Placement
      top: Top (e.g. Browser tabs)
      bottom: Bottom (e.g. iOS tab bars)
      vertical: Vertical (e.g. Edge vertical tabs)
      segmented-control: Segmented control (e.g. iOS segmented controls)
  - overflow (single-select: one id) — Overflow
      scroll: Scroll (e.g. Material scrollable tabs)
      shrink: Shrink (e.g. Chrome tabs)
      more-menu: More menu (e.g. Office ribbons)
      wrap: Wrap (e.g. Old desktop dialogs)
* Labels [content] — What does a tab say?
  - label (multi-select: list of ids) — Label content
      text: Text (e.g. GitHub repository tabs)
      icon: Icon (e.g. Bottom tab bars)
      badge-count: Badge count (e.g. Unread counts)
      favicon-and-title: Favicon and title (e.g. Browser tabs)
      close-button: Close button (e.g. Editor tabs)
* Tab origin and grouping [composition] — Who makes tabs, and can they be grouped?
  - origin (single-select: one id) — Origin
      fixed-by-the-designer: Fixed by the designer (e.g. Settings tabs)
      created-by-the-person: Created by the person (e.g. Browser tabs; CHI '25 probe overviews)
      saved-views: Saved views (e.g. Notion database views)
      pinned-and-preview-tabs: Pinned and preview tabs — A preview tab is replaced unless kept (e.g. VS Code preview tabs)
  - grouping (single-select: one id) — Grouping
      flat: Flat (e.g. Most tab sets)
      tab-groups: Tab groups (e.g. Chrome tab groups)
      nested-tabs: Nested tabs (e.g. Tabs inside a tab panel)
* Background tabs [lifecycle] — What happens to a tab you are not looking at?
  - background (single-select: one id) — Background state
      unloaded-on-switch: Unloaded on switch (e.g. Simple tab widgets)
      kept-alive: Kept alive (e.g. Editor tabs)
      put-to-sleep: Put to sleep (e.g. Edge sleeping tabs)
* Switching [invocation] — How does a person switch?
  - switchBy (multi-select: list of ids) — Switch by
      click: Click (e.g. All)
      swipe-between-panels: Swipe between panels (e.g. Android tab layouts)
      keyboard: Keyboard (e.g. Ctrl+Tab)
      search-tabs: Search tabs (e.g. Chrome tab search)

## carousel — Carousel (component, archetype browse-collections)
A horizontally scrolling strip that shows a subset of items at once and hides the rest off-screen.
Aliases: slider, shelf, horizontal scroller
Anatomy: Track (The items in order); Viewport (What is currently visible); Controls (Arrows, dots, swipe)
Related — uses: card, pagination | neighbors: stories, tabs
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Visible items [layout] — How many items are visible, and how?
  - visible (single-select: one id) — Visible items
      one-at-a-time: One at a time — A hero slide (e.g. Homepage hero carousels)
      peek-next: Peek next — The next item shows at the edge (e.g. App Store)
      multi-item-strip: Multi-item strip (e.g. Netflix rows)
      hero-with-smaller-neighbours: Hero with smaller neighbours (e.g. Material 3 hero carousel)
* Advancing [invocation] — How does it move?
  - advance (multi-select: list of ids) — Advance by
      swipe: Swipe (e.g. Mobile)
      arrow-buttons: Arrow buttons (e.g. Netflix on web)
      dots: Dots (e.g. Hero banners)
      autoplay: Autoplay (e.g. Marketing heroes)
* Timing [lifecycle] — Does it move on its own?
  - autoplay (single-select: one id) — Autoplay
      off: Off (e.g. Netflix)
      timed-pausing-on-interaction: Timed, pausing on interaction (e.g. Retail heroes)

## prompt-input — Prompt input (component, archetype delegate-ai)
The control where a person enters or edits the instruction, context and attachments sent to a model.
Aliases: composer, prompt box, AI text field
Anatomy: Text area (The instruction); Attachments (Files, images, selections); Submit (Send or run); Modifiers (Model, tools, parameters)
Related — neighbors: text-field, suggestion-chips, file-upload
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Input content [content] — What can the composer hold?
  - content (multi-select: list of ids) — Content
      plain-prompt: Plain prompt (e.g. ChatGPT box)
      mentions-of-files-or-symbols: Mentions of files or symbols (e.g. Cursor @)
      attached-images-or-docs: Attached images or docs (e.g. ChatGPT uploads)
      hidden-system-preamble: Hidden system preamble (e.g. Custom GPTs)
      parameter-flags: Parameter flags (e.g. Midjourney suffix)
* Composer layout [layout] — Where does the prompt UI sit?
  - layout (single-select: one id) — Layout
      bottom-sticky-composer: Bottom sticky composer (e.g. ChatGPT)
      inline-caret-popover: Inline caret popover (e.g. Cursor Cmd-K)
      modal-brief: Modal brief (e.g. Agent task dialogs)
      sidebar-composer: Sidebar composer (e.g. IDE chat panels)
      voice-first-with-transcript: Voice-first with transcript (e.g. Voice modes)
      centred-hero-box: Centred hero box — A large prompt box in the middle of an empty page that becomes the bottom composer once a thread starts (e.g. Perplexity — Ask anything box)
      terminal-prompt-line: Terminal prompt line — A readline-style input at the bottom of a terminal transcript, with slash commands and mentions typed in place (e.g. Claude Code — Prompt line)
* Submitting [invocation] — How is the prompt sent?
  - submitBy (multi-select: list of ids) — Submit by
      enter-key: Enter key (e.g. Chat UIs)
      click-send: Click send (e.g. All)
      push-to-talk: Push to talk (e.g. Voice)
      queue-while-running: Queue while running (e.g. Follow-ups mid-stream)
      schedule-send: Schedule send (e.g. Batch agents)
      open-mic: Open mic — Nothing is pressed or held to send — the microphone stays open and voice activity detection ends the turn, which is what separates modern voice modes from push-to-talk (e.g. ChatGPT — Voice mode screen)
* Composer assistance [initiative] — What help shapes the prompt before send?
  - assistance (multi-select: list of ids) — Assistance
      none: None (e.g. Bare text boxes)
      placeholder-examples: Placeholder examples (e.g. Chat onboarding)
      rewrite-my-prompt: Rewrite my prompt (e.g. Prompt improvers)
      suggestion-chips: Suggestion chips (e.g. Starter prompts)
      template-slots: Template slots (e.g. Fill-in briefs)

## text-field — Text field (component, archetype enter-data)
A single- or multi-line input for typed text, together with its label, help and validation.
Aliases: input, text box, text area
Anatomy: Label (What is asked); Input (Where text goes); Supporting text (Hint, counter or error)
Related — neighbors: autocomplete, inline-edit
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Supporting content [content] — What surrounds the input?
  - supporting (multi-select: list of ids) — Supporting content
      label: Label (e.g. All)
      placeholder: Placeholder (e.g. Search boxes)
      hint-text: Hint text (e.g. GOV.UK)
      character-counter: Character counter (e.g. Material text fields)
      prefix-or-suffix: Prefix or suffix (e.g. Currency and units)
      clear-button: Clear button (e.g. Search fields)
      format-examples: Format examples — A worked example of the expected format (e.g. QQ 12 34 56 C) shown alongside the field — the 'form' entry's Help dimension has this exact variation, but this entry's Supporting-content options don't. (e.g. GOV.UK — National Insurance number field)
